The script's APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS came only from the prnewswire.co.uk allowlist warning and its 403 bot-block; prnewswire.co.uk was independently confirmed as PR Newswire/Cision's UK domain (identical release ID 302942093 also published on the already-allowlisted prnewswire.com) and added to config/source_allowlist.txt, the release content was read via that mirror, and every claim, number, attribution and hedged figure in the article traced cleanly to the three cited sources with no fabrication or misattribution.

findings.details: prnewswire.co.uk returned HTTP 403 to the automated fetcher and to a direct curl with a browser User-Agent; no Archive.org capture exists for the URL (wayback availability API returned an empty archived_snapshots object). The identical press release (release ID 302942093) is published at the same path on prnewswire.com, which is already allowlisted and returned HTTP 200. Fetched that mirror directly (sha256 4889799cdfd99a65185ba98963bd9ee1352c611e496ab686dcb36838c897afda of the raw HTML), confirming prnewswire.co.uk is PR Newswire/Cision's UK-market domain for the same wire release, not a third-party mirror. Added prnewswire.co.uk to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment in this review's commit. All claims attributed to the press release in the article were verified against this mirrored content.

content_preview.title: Isomorphic Labs Raises $5 Billion Series C as Alphabet-Backed AI Drug Discovery Lab Pushes Toward Clinical Trials
content_preview.summary: The DeepMind spinout, led by Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis, raised $5 billion six months after a $2.1 billion Series B, with Alphabet still its controlling investor.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery company spun out of Google's DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 billion in a Series C funding round as it works to move its AI-designed drug candidates into clinical trials, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/isomorphic-labs-raises-5b-as-it-looks-to-take-drug-candidates-to-clinical-trials/). The round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with new investor Andreessen Horowitz joining alongside continued participatio...

recommendations: Resolved during manual review: prnewswire.co.uk added to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment; no corrections record needed since no content inaccuracy was found (see editor_notes).

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece on Isomorphic Labs' $5B Series C (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). Appropriate depth for a business/biotech audience, neutral tone, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. The writer disclosed on the PR that it deliberately excluded direct quotes from company executives after two WebFetch passes on the press release produced inconsistent 'verbatim' text; I independently verified this caution was warranted (see source_verification) and that the final article contains zero quotes attributed to any named executive — the only quoted fragment is the short phrase 'positive preclinical results,' which is attributed generically to 'the company... according to TechCrunch,' not to a person, and is verbatim in both the TechCrunch snapshot and the press release.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources verified. (1) source-0.html.gz (TechCrunch, Ram Iyer, Nov 17 2026, HTTP 200, sha256 matches manifest) — confirms the $5B Series C, Greenoaks/Sequoia Capital co-lead, Andreessen Horowitz as new investor, existing backers (GV, CapitalG, Thrive Capital, MGX, Temasek, UK Sovereign AI Fund), the IsoDDE drug-design engine built on AlphaFold, the verbatim quoted phrase 'positive preclinical results' in oncology and immunology, the Eli Lilly/Novartis/Johnson & Johnson deals, the $2.1B Series B in May, Hassabis stepping down as head of DeepMind to a chairman role (his 'first fundraise since' framing matches TechCrunch's wording almost exactly), the Hassabis/Jumper Nobel Prize in chemistry for AlphaFold, and that Isomorphic did not disclose a new valuation while Bloomberg had reported a ~$50B valuation-talk figure earlier in the month, not confirmed by TechCrunch. (2) source-1.html.gz (R&D World, Brian Buntz, Nov 17 2026, HTTP 200, sha256 matches manifest) — confirms the same funding/investor facts, 'Alphabet holds 75% or more of Isomorphic's shares and voting rights, according to UK Companies House records that reflect a June share allotment' (quoted near-verbatim in the article), BioSpace's tally of 'at least $7.7 billion raised by Isomorphic since March 2025,' BioSpace calling the round the largest venture round in biotech history surpassing the $3B Altos Labs raised at its 2022 launch, the Bloomberg Nov. 4 report of talks at a ~$50B valuation, and that 'Hassabis said at Davos in January that Isomorphic expected its first clinical trials by the end of 2026, Reuters reported' — the article correctly frames this as Reuters reporting relayed by R&D World rather than claiming direct Herald verification of the Reuters report. (3) prnewswire.co.uk (the Isomorphic Labs press release) failed to snapshot: HTTP 403 to the automated fetcher and to a direct curl with a browser User-Agent; no Wayback capture exists (checked via the archive.org availability API — empty archived_snapshots). Read it instead via the identical release (ID 302942093) mirrored on the already-allowlisted prnewswire.com (HTTP 200, sha256 4889799cdfd99a65185ba98963bd9ee1352c611e496ab686dcb36838c897afda of the fetched HTML). That mirror confirms every claim the article attributes to the press release: the investor list verbatim ('all existing investors: Thrive Capital, MGX, GV, CapitalG, Temasek and the UK Sovereign AI Fund'), the IsoDDE description, the London/Cambridge MA/Lausanne offices, and — critically — four direct quotes from named executives (Demis Hassabis, President Max Jaderberg, Greenoaks' Neil Mehta, Sequoia's Konstantine Buhler) that exist in the release in full paragraph form. None of these four quotes appear anywhere in the submitted article, confirming the writer's stated exclusion was accurate and that no fabricated or inconsistent 'verbatim' quote slipped through. prnewswire.co.uk independently confirmed as PR Newswire/Cision's UK-market domain (same release ID as the US domain, same publisher, same wire-service formatting) and added to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment in this review's commit — this resolves the only two automated findings. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic appears only once, in an incidental aside ('Jumper has since left DeepMind for Anthropic') linking to prior Herald coverage; the article is not about Anthropic or an Anthropic product, does not name Anthropic in the headline/summary/lead, and contains no Anthropic/Claude credit line.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabrications, no hallucinated quotes, no misattribution found. The $50 billion valuation figure — the one specifically flagged for scrutiny — is correctly handled throughout: the article states plainly that 'Isomorphic did not disclose a new valuation,' that the $50B number comes from 'a Bloomberg report earlier in November' relayed by TechCrunch and R&D World, that neither outlet 'confirmed [it] independently of the Bloomberg report,' and the 'What We Don't Know' section restates that the figure 'traces to a Bloomberg report on funding talks rather than a confirmed number.' This matches both snapshots exactly (TechCrunch: 'Isomorphic did not disclose its new valuation. Bloomberg reported earlier this month that the lab was looking to raise funding at a $50 billion valuation'; R&D World: 'Bloomberg had reported Nov. 4 that the company was in talks to raise about $5 billion at a valuation of roughly $50 billion') — the article never states $50B as a company-confirmed fact. Ran the claim-accuracy quantifier scan (grep for absence/quantifier terms) across the submission body: the 'all of the company's existing investors' claim, the 'first fundraise since' claim, and the '75% or more' / '$7.7 billion' / '$3 billion Altos Labs' figures all trace verbatim to the cited sources. Derived/vendor figures (75% stake, $7.7B cumulative, $3B Altos Labs comparison) are each labelled to their original attributor (Companies House via R&D World; BioSpace via R&D World) rather than stated as the Herald's own calculation. No headline/summary/lead claim is unsourced; all are directly backed by the TechCrunch and press-release snapshots.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Attribution phrases ('according to TechCrunch,' 'according to the press release,' 'R&D World also reported') are used consistently to separate reporting from the Herald's own framing. No sensationalism despite the record-setting ('largest venture round in biotech history') framing, which is explicitly attributed to BioSpace via R&D World rather than asserted by the Herald.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior Isomorphic Labs coverage; none found. Related but non-duplicate prior Herald coverage: the April 2026 OpenAI GPT-Rosalind drug-discovery article (different company/story) and the June 2026 John Jumper/Anthropic departure article (directly referenced via internal link in this submission's body, confirmed to resolve to a real published article). This is a new topic, not a rewrite or duplicate of existing coverage.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced News coverage of a real $5B funding round with no fabricated or misattributed claims; the writer's decision to exclude all direct executive quotes after detecting inconsistent WebFetch extractions was verified as warranted (the press release does contain four substantial named-executive quotes, none of which leaked into the article in any form), and the $50B valuation figure is correctly and consistently presented as an unconfirmed, Bloomberg-sourced figure rather than fact. The only automated findings were a missing allowlist entry and a bot-blocked snapshot for the press release, both resolved through independent verification via an allowlisted mirror. Featured candidacy: 2 - a record-setting, widely-covered funding round (the largest venture round in biotech history per BioSpace) for a DeepMind spinout led by a Nobel laureate, of interest to a broad business/tech audience, though it is a funding milestone rather than a scientific or product breakthrough.
